description: Access permissions are not organized by roles or groups; instead, individual permissions are assigned ad-hoc to users without a structured role-based framework. This signal indicates that access management lacks systematic organization, making it difficult to maintain consistent permissions, audit access, or enforce least privilege principles.
applicability: This signal applies to: Cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, GCP) Identity and access management systems Enterprise applications Database management systems Kubernetes and container orchestration Source code repositories Business intelligence and analytics platforms Content management systems Network and security appliances

metadata.detection_notes: Detection of this signal typically involves: Analyzing IAM configurations for role definitions Reviewing user-permission mappings for patterns Examining access control models in applications Auditing permission assignment histories Evaluating group and role utilization metrics Role-based access control (RBAC) is a best practice that: Simplifies permission management Ensures consistent access policies Supports audit and compliance requirements Enables efficient onboarding and offboarding Reduces the risk of permission creep The absence of RBAC often indicates technical debt in access management that becomes more difficult to remediate as systems grow.
